Amasra is a Black Sea port town and the cruise port to BartÄ±n City, both part of Turkey's BartÄ±n Province. Amasra has population around 7,000, while BartÄ±n (Province's capital) has population around 60,000. The road distance between Asra and Bartin is approx 13 km (8 mi) with tourist travel options buses and taxis.

As cruise port, Bartin-Amasra is visited mainly by top-luxury ships and superyachts.

Amasra is also visited by the cruise ship Astoria Grande/fka AIDAcara arriving from homeport Sochi Russia (via Istanbul) and also visiting Sinop. In 2022, Astoria Grande's schedule included 5x visits to Amasra (Sept 14 & 28, Oct 5, 12 & 19) with port stay between 8 am - 6 pm.

Port Bartin (locode TRBTN) is on the Black Sea while the city is located inland (on BartÄ±n River/navigable waterway) which allows access to the city directly from the Black Sea (approx 14 km / 9 mi sailing upstream) via smaller-sized ships, superyachts and boats. The settlement (as Parthenios/Parthenia) was established as an Ancient Greek colony, and later became part of the Imperium Romanum/Roman Empire, the Byzantium/Eastern Roman Empire and in the late-14th-century (1392) part of the Ottoman Empire (1299-1923).

Port Amasra (locode TRAMA) was also founded by the Greeks under the name Amastris, and is mentioned in Homer's Iliad (aka Song of Ilion) together with three other Ionian colonies (Cromna, Sesamus, Cytorus). Amasra is popular for its Archaeological Museum (located on the waterfront) which has ruins both on land and underwater. Other tourist attractions include Amasra Castle (built by the Romans, fortified by the Byzantines and the Genoese), Fatih Mosque (9th-century Byzantine church), the KuskayasÄ± Monument (akak Bird's Rock Road Monument/built by the Roman Governor Gaius Julius Aquila during the reign of Emperor Tiberius Claudius).

In 2018 started the TL 78 million (USD 4,3m) project for building the new Amasra cruise port. In August 2022, the project was ~90% completed.

Amasra is a compact Black Sea town where the principal sights, castle lanes, harbours and beaches fit comfortably into a half-day visit. Sightseeing is easy independently, although the historic quarters include slopes, steps and uneven paving.

Getting from the Cruise Port

Most current cruise calls berth at Amasra Passenger Port on the eastern side of Büyük Liman. After completing port formalities, passengers can normally walk into the centre; the waterfront and first shops are roughly 1 km (0.6 mi) away, or about 10–20 minutes on foot.

Some smaller-ship itineraries may use a different landing arrangement or identify the call as Amasra/Bartın, so confirm the actual arrival point and any shuttle information onboard. A vehicle is unnecessary for central Amasra but essential for Safranbolu and other regional excursions.

Best Ways to Spend Your Time

Amasra Castle and Boztepe

Allow 2–3 hours to explore the inhabited castle district, its surviving gates and walls, Kemere Bridge and the lanes of Boztepe. The elevated sections provide the best views across the two harbours. This is practical independently, but expect inclines, steps and irregular stone surfaces.

Harbours, Museum and Local Market

For a gentler visit, follow the Büyük Liman waterfront into town, browse the wooden crafts and souvenirs in Çekiciler Bazaar, and continue toward Amasra Museum and Küçük Liman. Allow around 2 hours, longer if visiting the museum or stopping for lunch. Check the museum’s opening status locally before relying on a visit.

Beach or Waterfront Lunch

Büyük Liman and Küçük Liman beaches are both within the central sightseeing area. A short beach stop can therefore be combined with the castle walk without arranging transport. Swimming conditions depend on Black Sea weather, and facilities may be limited outside the summer season. Waterfront restaurants are convenient for local fish and Amasra salad, but leave extra time when several tour groups are ashore.

Safranbolu

The UNESCO-listed Ottoman town of Safranbolu is approximately 95–100 km (59.0–62.1 mi) inland, normally around 1.5 hours each way by road. Its preserved houses, market lanes and historic public buildings make it the main full-day excursion from Amasra.

An organized excursion or prearranged private vehicle is recommended. Ordinary public transport involves too much uncertainty for a cruise call. The round trip consumes at least 3 hours before sightseeing, so Safranbolu suits a long port stay rather than a short call.

Self-Guided Amasra Walking Tour

Harbours and Castle Circuit

Distance: approximately 3.5 km (2.2 mi). Pure walking time: about 60–75 minutes. Recommended total time: 2.5–3.5 hours. Difficulty: moderate, with slopes, stairs and uneven paving.

  1. Passenger-port exit: Follow the harbour road toward central Amasra.
  2. Büyük Liman: Walk beside the main bay and beach toward the town centre.
  3. Çekiciler Bazaar: Browse the compact market area known for locally made wooden items and souvenirs.
  4. Castle lanes: Enter the old quarter and follow the narrow streets through the surviving fortifications.
  5. Kemere Bridge: Cross the historic stone bridge linking the mainland castle section with Boztepe.
  6. Boztepe: Continue uphill through the residential lanes for coastal and harbour views.
  7. Küçük Liman: Descend toward the smaller harbour, beach and Amasra Museum area.
  8. Return: Walk through the modern centre and along Büyük Liman to the passenger port.

The circuit can be shortened by omitting the higher Boztepe lanes. Passengers with limited mobility may prefer the relatively level waterfront, bazaar and museum area; the castle itself is less accessible.

Practical Tips

  • Wear shoes suitable for polished stone, steps and steep lanes.
  • Carry some Turkish lira for small shops, cafés and local transport, even though cards are widely accepted at larger businesses.
  • Summer weekends can bring heavy road traffic and crowded waterfront areas.
  • Do not plan a distant trip by unreserved taxi or public transport without confirming the return journey first.
  • Allow at least 45–60 minutes between finishing independent sightseeing and the ship’s all-aboard time, with a larger margin after Safranbolu or another road excursion.
